fn wechat_profile::file_resource_type | fn(extension: &str) -> u32 | Resource categories from the supported Linux build's extension registry. An unknown extension uses its observed generic category; these are file resource types, independently of the file hardlink table's constant type 1. Supported Linux 4.1.13.26 AMD64: registry 0x7554e70, classifier 0x7558600, resource constructors 0x755c1ca/0x755d66f (category << 16 | 3).

fn wechat_profile::initialize_profile | fn(path: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, password: &[u8]) -> wechat_profile::Result<(wechat_profile::snapshot::ProfileLocation, wechat_profile::keys::KeyFile, wechat_profile::initialize::InitializedLayout)> | Creates a NEW account root atomically. The caller supplies an existing/new 32-byte binary database password explicitly and stores returned keys separately. For an official home this is the accepted account AuthSect field 9 payload; generating another password cannot substitute for that server-issued value. This initializes ordinary native schemas; it does not claim a fully trusted login profile or manufacture custom-tokenizer indexes.

This never calls the old database initializer/migrator or any key acquisition process. The agent token is an unlock passphrase, not an exported profile key or network credential.

No password discovery, fallback, account switch, or source mutation takes place; the password itself is not retained in the result.
fn wechat_profile::mark_read_messages | fn(location: &wechat_profile::snapshot::ProfileLocation, keys: &wechat_profile::keys::KeyFile, thread: &str, ids: &[wechat_profile::model::SourceMessageId], options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::writer::ReadProjection> | Project only the selected source-qualified incoming observations. This is desktop-local state: it neither acknowledges consumer events nor sends a read receipt to the phone. Counter/list discrepancies already present are retained by subtracting only removed rows rather than rebuilding from list cardinality.
fn wechat_profile::mark_read_thread | fn(location: &wechat_profile::snapshot::ProfileLocation, keys: &wechat_profile::keys::KeyFile, thread: &str, through_time: i64, options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::thread_read::ThreadReadProjection> | Clear this session through a frozen server timestamp, preserving later rows. Unlike an exact-ID projection, this reconciles an older counter/list mismatch when the entire known session is before the boundary. It performs no RPC.

Missing, hidden and excluded sessions remain unchanged. The caller must retain the full control as incomplete and journal every evaluated result.

None means a new file, never permission to overwrite unknown contents. The coordinator journals/retries this step under its exclusive profile lease.
fn wechat_profile::publish_mmkv_append | fn(path: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, staged: &wechat_profile::mmkv::StagedMmkv, options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::mmkv::MmkvPublication> | Publish a previously staged append while the caller holds exclusive profile ownership and its durable intent. Data is replaced first: the old metadata still validates the unchanged ciphertext prefix. Metadata publication exposes the new span. Replay accepts the intermediate new-data/old-metadata state. This is not atomic with database, credential or sidecar cursor transactions.
fn wechat_profile::publish_mmkv_append_guarded | fn(path: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, staged: &wechat_profile::mmkv::StagedMmkv, options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions, allowed: impl core::ops::function::FnMut() -> bool) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::mmkv::MmkvPublication> | Recheck an external authorization fence before each independent data/metadata commit. If the fence closes between commits, the caller retains its sealed intent and the ordinary append replay rules accept the data-first state.
fn wechat_profile::publish_mmkv_create | fn(path: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, staged: &wechat_profile::mmkv::StagedMmkv, options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::mmkv::MmkvPublication> | Publish a journaled newly created pair without replacing any existing bytes. Replay accepts only exact staged files, including a data-only crash state. The caller must authorize the missing store (e.g. its managed bootstrap receipt) and create/own the canonical parent directory before calling this function.
fn wechat_profile::publish_saved_key_info | fn(home: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, username: &str, plan: &wechat_profile::login_storage::SavedKeyInfoPlan, bytes: &[u8], options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::login_storage::SavedKeyInfoPublication> | Publish native-shaped key-info, retaining unrelated accounts/history. The inspected writer supplies key_md5='' (not a digest of the new credential). Its known UNIQUE(user_name_md5,key_info_md5) tuple is replaced only when the older tuple contains identical bytes and the same native empty key_md5. If no DB exists, use the native raw legacy fallback without inventing a DB.
fn wechat_profile::publish_saved_key_info_guarded | fn(home: impl core::convert::AsRef<std::path::Path>, username: &str, plan: &wechat_profile::login_storage::SavedKeyInfoPlan, bytes: &[u8], options: &wechat_profile::writer::WriteOptions, allowed: impl core::ops::function::FnMut() -> bool) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::login_storage::SavedKeyInfoPublication> | The coordinator must recheck its authorization fence immediately before each independently durable publication. A false guard preserves the caller's encrypted intent for replay; it cannot roll back an earlier committed file.

fn wechat_profile::stage_mmkv_values | fn(data: &[u8], metadata: &[u8], key: &[u8], updates: &[(alloc::string::String, core::option::Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>)]) -> wechat_profile::Result<wechat_profile::mmkv::StagedMmkv> | Append while preserving IV/sequence/flags and the complete old ciphertext prefix. A full data file grows to the next 4096-byte page, at most 4 MiB; records are never compacted or discarded. Identical values are byte-idempotent. Values are already MMKV-encoded; None is a tombstone. fn wechat_profile::verify_profile_password | fn(location: &wechat_profile::snapshot::ProfileLocation, keys: &wechat_profile::keys::KeyFile, password: &[u8]) -> wechat_profile::Result<usize> | Confirm a server-issued account database password against every actual DB header and the already authorized page-key map. Only 4096-byte headers are read; SQLite never opens these files, and no key/password bytes are returned. The caller must hold exclusive profile ownership or supply a stopped copy. Missing coverage, a different salt generation or one mismatched key fails closed. This does not rekey, repair, replace or switch the attached profile.
